title: AI Security Agent
tagline: Catch confidential data before it is pasted into an AI chatbot.
summary: Network-level data-loss prevention for AI usage. A TLS-inspecting proxy spots prompts headed to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other AI services, scans them for secrets, credentials and personal data, and reports redacted findings to a SIEM-style admin dashboard.
problem: Employees paste source code, API keys and customer data into AI tools every day, and browser-extension monitors miss API calls and non-browser apps entirely. A network control sees all of it, and mirrors the SSL-inspection model organizations already run on their firewalls.
approach: A mitmproxy add-on matches each request by host and path against a registry of known AI services, then uses a per-provider extractor to pull out only the text the user typed — not system prompts, earlier turns or analytics beacons. Events are delivered on a worker thread, so a slow backend can never stall a user's request.
A DLP engine scores that text on a 1 to 10 scale. It detects AWS keys, GitHub and Slack tokens, private key blocks, JWTs, SSNs, Luhn-validated card numbers and confidential-marker keywords.

The detector is redaction-first: it never stores or returns the raw match, so the monitoring tool cannot become a new store of secrets. The admin dashboard shows only the risk summary, data types and counts. The consent model is disclosure through acceptable-use policy with a silent runtime, and it is documented in the repo.
highlights: Validated on live traffic, not just unit tests: real requests to the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs, plus real browser sessions on Gemini and Perplexity, through a local test proxy. The test CA was never installed system-wide.

Found and fixed a real gap: the first browser test recorded zero events, because chat UIs use their own request formats — Gemini nests JSON inside JSON inside a form field. Endpoint-aware parsers now catch them.
Perplexity echoes each prompt into analytics beacons. The registry matches on path, so the beacons are ignored and a prompt is reported exactly once.
Redaction by design: findings carry the rule, category and weight — never the secret itself.
Admin dashboard with summary tiles, breakdowns by AI service and data type, filters, per-event rationale and live refresh, in light and dark mode.
56 automated tests across the DLP engine, extractors, proxy add-on and backend. A small capture tool records request structure — never prompt text — for building new parsers.
next: Capture ChatGPT and Claude web traffic from a signed-in session. ChatGPT blocks automated browsers, and claude.ai needs a login, so those parsers are written but unverified.
Inspect Microsoft Copilot, which chats over a WebSocket rather than plain requests.
Authentication, plus a per-device drill-down and trend charts in the dashboard.
Root CA and PAC/GPO deployment tooling, with certificate-pinning checks, then multi-tenant separation.
